audit_kind: read-only performance bottleneck audit (no code/config/output modified)

evidence_basis.static_audit: 5 read-only subagents read every stage module fully; no multiprocessing anywhere in src/ (grep-confirmed)

candidates.title: Flip distance.recompute true->false; load cached parquet instead of rebuilding networkx graph every run
candidates.profiling_evidence: tte.yaml sets recompute:true; build_or_load short-circuit at distance.py:235 never fires; production cache already exists (data/processed/fifth_ring/tte/cluster_network_distance.parquet = 140 KB). Entries 7-13 of TTE audit (graph rebuild, collapse_min_undirected, build_filtered_subgraph, pick_representatives, C Dijkstra SSSPs) all execute unnecessarily.
candidates.current_complexity: O(C * (|V| log|V| + |E|)) per run for C Dijkstra SSSPs + O(|E|) python collapse; C=100, OSM graph city-scale
candidates.proposed_fix: Set recompute:false (or remove key). build_or_load becomes a single pd.read_parquet of the 140 KB CxC matrix.
candidates.expected_gain: Eliminates the entire graph-rebuild portion of TTE wall. The standalone path (tte.py:682-683) already forbids recompute=true when fallback files exist, confirming intended posture is load-not-rebuild.
candidates.extra_memory: none (140 KB read vs full graph load)
candidates.determinism_risk: none - cached matrix is byte-identical (forced symmetric at distance.py:214, zero diagonal)
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - identical matrix returned

candidates.title: Cache STRtree on segments once; reuse across all chunks and pickup/dropoff (currently rebuilt ~360 times)
candidates.profiling_evidence: sjoin_nearest rebuilds the right-frame STRtree on every call; 180 chunks x 2 (pickup+dropoff) = ~360 builds of the full 59096-segment index. Demand audit B2. Demand is the 70m stage (largest).
candidates.current_complexity: O(chunks * 2 * (S log S index build + P_chunk log S query)); S=59096, P_chunk=500000, chunks=180
candidates.proposed_fix: Pre-build segments[['seg_id','geometry']] and persist its .sindex once before the chunk loop; reuse for both pickup and dropoff. Or build a shapely STRtree directly and query it.
candidates.expected_gain: High - removes the dominant CPU term of the 70m Demand stage (360 redundant O(S log S) builds + 360 Point list-comprehension constructions of up to 500k points each).
candidates.extra_memory: one persistent STRtree + one segment GeoDataFrame view (small vs OD tensor)
candidates.parallel_safety: n/a for the fix itself; is prerequisite for safe chunk parallelism (DEM-17)
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - current tie-break is gpd.sjoin_nearest + drop_duplicates('row_id') (geospatial.py:331), which depends on tree-build/traversal order; a pre-built/reordered index can reassign equidistant orders to a different seg_id. Must enforce an explicit deterministic tie-break (e.g. lowest seg_id string) on ties.
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: HIGH unless a deterministic tie-break is added; origin/destination_cluster_id and the OD tensor could change for tie cases. Validate against golden/baseline before merging.

candidates.title: Vectorize OD tensor fill via np scatter instead of itertuples python loop
candidates.profiling_evidence: itertuples loop fills dense tensors; each (slot,o,d) key is unique (SQL GROUP BY result) so last-writer-wins is a no-op. Demand audit B4.
candidates.current_complexity: O(R) python iterations; R = distinct (slot,o,d) OD rows, ~10^5-10^6
candidates.proposed_fix: Vectorized scatter: tensors[name][slots, O, D] = counts via numpy fancy indexing, using a np.where mask to preserve the dict.get drop-unmapped behavior.
candidates.expected_gain: Low-moderate wall; removes a python-level loop in the 70m stage.
candidates.determinism_risk: none (int32 assignment, no reduction)
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: low - must preserve the silent drop of unmapped keys (np.where mask); otherwise exactly equivalent

candidates.title: Drop redundant trip_segments sort (already sorted by same key upstream)
candidates.profiling_evidence: build_trip_segments already sorts by [driver_id,trip_start,trip_end,segment_id] at :198; reconstruct_driver_chains re-sorts by the identical key at :230. Supply audit B6.
candidates.current_complexity: O(N log N) redundant mergesort per block
candidates.proposed_fix: Remove the sort at :230 (keep the :273 chain_id sort - different key, genuinely needed).
candidates.expected_gain: low; removes one O(N log N) pass over 46M rows total across 8 blocks
candidates.determinism_risk: none - upstream sort already produces the same total order; mergesort stability preserved
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - identical row order

candidates.title: Gate serialize_list_columns .copy() behind list-column presence
candidates.profiling_evidence: output = frame.copy() runs unconditionally before every gzip write; the three production supply tables are pure scalar (no order_ids/segment_ids list columns) so the copy is pure overhead. Supply audit B4.
candidates.current_complexity: O(rows) extra peak memory per write; available/fleet frames are T*N = 1.32M rows each
candidates.proposed_fix: Only copy when a list column is actually present; else pass frame through.
candidates.expected_gain: low wall; removes a per-write RSS spike on the dense available/fleet frames
candidates.determinism_risk: none
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - no list columns to serialize for scalar tables

candidates.title: Switch np.add.at -> buffered A[t,i,j]+=vals (indices duplicate-free per call)
candidates.profiling_evidence: each block's compute_in_service_od already aggregated to one row per unique (slot,origin,dest), so within one np.add.at call there are no duplicate (t,i,j) indices; the unbuffered scatter is unnecessary. Supply audit B10.
candidates.current_complexity: O(K) unbuffered scatter-add into dense [T,N,N] target per block (cache-unfriendly)
candidates.proposed_fix: Use direct A[t,i,j] += vals (buffered) since indices are duplicate-free within a call.
candidates.expected_gain: low-moderate; measurably faster scatter into the 1.06 GiB dense accumulator
candidates.determinism_risk: none - integer addition
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - same integer sums

candidates.title: Dense in-service accumulator int64 -> int32 (code's own range-check proves int32 suffices)
candidates.profiling_evidence: A = np.zeros((T,N,N), dtype=np.int64); the guard at 789-791 raises if values exceed int32 max, proving int32 always suffices. Supply audit B1. T=13248, N=100 -> A is 1.06 GiB at int64, 0.53 GiB at int32.
candidates.proposed_fix: Allocate A as np.int32. (B/Fc int64 -> int32 where guards allow.)
candidates.expected_gain: halves the resident in-service accumulator (~0.53 GiB freed); lowers Supply RSS floor
candidates.determinism_risk: none - integer values fit int32 by the existing guard
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - contract reads CSV values as int64 regardless; values unchanged

candidates.title: Pre-build STRtree on ordinary segments once before the order chunk loop (rebuilt 2x per chunk)
candidates.profiling_evidence: match_points_to_segments_with_distance slices ordinary[['seg_id','geometry']] into a fresh GeoDataFrame each call, discarding the lazily-cached .sindex; 2 calls/chunk over the October order file. Preparation audit A2/D1.
candidates.current_complexity: O(chunks * 2 * (S log S build)); S = ordinary segment count (~tens of thousands)
candidates.proposed_fix: Pre-slice and pre-build .sindex on ordinary once; reuse across all chunks.
candidates.expected_gain: moderate fraction of the 6m Preparation wall; same pattern as DEM-01
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - same sjoin_nearest tie-break concern as DEM-01; needs deterministic tie-break
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM without tie-break; order feature counts could shift for equidistant orders. Validate vs frozen_inputs.

candidates.title: Pass POI/order DataFrames directly to relation-graph builder instead of round-tripping through CSV
candidates.profiling_evidence: _build_relation_graph re-reads poi_features.csv and order_features.csv that _build_poi_features/_build_order_features just wrote moments earlier in the same run(). Preparation audit B2.
candidates.current_complexity: O(N*C) disk read + reparse twice; doubles RSS transiently (CSV-derived frame coexists with in-memory frame)
candidates.proposed_fix: Thread the in-memory DataFrames through to _build_relation_graph instead of re-reading.
candidates.expected_gain: low-moderate; removes 2 disk reads + reparses + a transient RSS double-occupancy
candidates.determinism_risk: none - same data, no transform
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - identical

candidates.title: Vectorize POI entropy + per-edge cosine similarity (matmul) instead of row-by-row numpy
candidates.profiling_evidence: features['poi_entropy'] = [_entropy(row) for row in ...]; per-edge loop calls _cosine (np.linalg.norm + np.dot) per edge when composition/order_vectors are already dense matrices. Preparation audit B1/B4.
candidates.current_complexity: O(N*C) entropy + O(E) per-edge cosine; E = relation edges (~tens of thousands)
candidates.proposed_fix: Vectorize entropy across rows; compute all cosines as composition @ composition.T then index by edge pairs.
candidates.expected_gain: low-moderate
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - BLAS matmul changes FP summation order -> ~1e-15 differences in entropy/cosine; CSV writes 6+ sig figs so bytes can change. preparation.py:374 manifest reuse compares sha256 of outputs, so byte-identity matters for cache hits.
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - checksums/manifest hashes may drift unless results are rounded to fixed precision before writing

candidates.title: Drop redundant full-objective recompute after every accepted move (move_delta already gives incremental delta)
candidates.profiling_evidence: objective_components walks every graph edge from scratch after each accepted move, even though move_delta (objective.py:129-179) already computed the O(degree) incremental delta. Only used for trace row + 1e-8 invariant guard. Partition audit B1. Canonical run = 1 init x 1 setting, so the 3.5m is dominated by a single run_search.
candidates.current_complexity: O(M * E) per run_search; M = accepted moves (up to N*max_passes), E = graph edges
candidates.proposed_fix: Keep move_delta for acceptance; replace per-move full recompute with periodic snapshots for the trace + invariant (or recompute only the invariant periodically).
candidates.expected_gain: moderate-to-high fraction of the 3.5m Partition wall (primary cost)
candidates.determinism_risk: the 1e-8 invariant guard at search.py:566 ties incremental acceptance to the full recompute; any reordering must keep the tolerance or risk false-positive RuntimeError
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - the objective_trace.csv 'accepted_delta' and component columns must stay bit-identical; the final partition is unchanged (same moves accepted)

candidates.title: Within-hop column parallelism over nan_cols (frozen-snapshot design makes it output-equivalent)
candidates.profiling_evidence: each iteration reads only frozen round-start snapshots (source_value/support_src, tte.py:381-382) and writes only its own column of value_cur (:409); no intra-hop cross-column dependency. TTE audit entry 1. This is the dominant 12m compute (after TTE-01 removes the rebuild).
candidates.current_complexity: O(R * M * K * T) single-threaded; R=3 hops, M=C^2=10000, K~100, T=13248
candidates.proposed_fix: Thread or process pool over nan_cols within each hop; rounds stay sequential (hop-depth dependency).
candidates.expected_gain: high - near-linear scaling of the dominant TTE compute across cores
candidates.extra_memory: per-worker column slice (small if columns are independent)
candidates.parallel_safety: safe - frozen snapshots are read-only within a hop; writes are column-disjoint
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - np.argmin over candidates (tte.py:297) returns first min on ties; a parallel/unordered min-reduction could pick a different candidate -> different support_min. Use argmin-with-index preserving first-min.
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - must preserve first-min argmin tie-break and frozen-snapshot semantics; column processing order within a hop does not affect results

candidates.title: Cache get_candidates across rounds (candidate set is invariant across hops)
candidates.code_location: src/roadnet_partition/downstream/tte.py:175-192 (get_candidates), called per still-NaN column per round
candidates.profiling_evidence: candidate set depends only on fixed (O,D, distance matrix, detour_ratio) - invariant across rounds - yet is recomputed every round for each still-NaN column. TTE audit entry 15.
candidates.current_complexity: O(R * M * K) recomputations of an invariant
candidates.proposed_fix: Precompute candidate lists once per OD column before the round loop.
candidates.expected_gain: low-moderate
candidates.determinism_risk: none - get_candidates builds list via np.where (ascending index order); cache preserves order
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none

candidates.title: Parallelize the (initialization x setting) search grid (embarrassingly parallel, resume-keyed)
candidates.profiling_evidence: nested for initialization / for setting loops run run_search serially; each writes independent output files and shares only read-only inputs. Partition audit B6. Canonical run is 1x1 so this helps only wider grids.
candidates.current_complexity: O(|inits| * |settings|) sequential run_search
candidates.proposed_fix: ProcessPool over settings; fork-based to inherit the read-only nx.Graph + demand dict without pickling.
candidates.expected_gain: near-linear for wide grids; ~none for canonical 1x1 run
candidates.extra_memory: per-worker graph copy if not fork-based (the ~11 GiB RSS contributor) - use fork
candidates.parallel_safety: safe - independent outputs, resume-keyed by (algorithm, setting_id); no double-write
candidates.determinism_risk: none - each run independent and seeded/sorted
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none

candidates.title: Sparsify the dense OD tensor (3x int32 (T,C,C) = 1.59 GiB) to COO/CSR
candidates.profiling_evidence: Y_exclusive/Y_carpool/Y_total are fully zero-allocated then densified; the OD is extremely sparse. Demand audit B1. At C=100 each tensor is ~0.53 GiB (3 = 1.59 GiB); scales as O(C^2). Primary contributor to the 11.2 GiB peak RSS.
candidates.current_complexity: O(T * C^2) memory, 3 tensors
candidates.proposed_fix: Store as scipy.sparse COO/CSR per slot or a flat (slot,o,d,excl,carpool) coordinate array.
candidates.expected_gain: RSS: GiB-scale -> MiB-scale; largest single memory win
candidates.determinism_risk: none - int32 sums, no reduction
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: HIGH - demand_contracts.validate_od_and_tensor (demand_contracts.py:154-176) and the TTE consumer assert tensor[name].shape == (T,C,C) and dtype==int32; sparse format requires a contract change + TTE consumer update

candidates.title: Chunk-level parallelism for order matching (180 independent chunks)
candidates.profiling_evidence: 180 CSV chunks are independent (each -> independent spatial match -> independent to_sql append). Demand audit B3. No multiprocessing anywhere in src/.
candidates.current_complexity: O(N) serial; N=90.1M orders
candidates.proposed_fix: Per-worker chunk slices; fork-inherited read-only segments + segment_to_cluster dict; per-worker SQLite shards or Parquet shards merged after.
candidates.expected_gain: near-linear chunk parallelism on the 70m stage
candidates.extra_memory: per-worker segments copy unless fork/COW; SQLite connection is not process-safe -> per-worker files
candidates.parallel_safety: safe if each worker has own SQLite connection; stats accumulation needs thread/process-safe merge
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - sjoin_nearest tie-break (DEM-01) must be identical per worker; identical segments row order guarantees this. ORDER BY driver_id,departure_time_ns,finish_time_ns,stage_id (demand.py:515-527) is load-bearing for carpool labels - must preserve including stage_id tiebreak
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - must preserve staging sort + service_label_batches (demand.py:101-122) ordering or carpool/exclusive labels could flip

candidates.title: Per-block sparse COO accumulators reduced once (enables both RSS win and block parallelism)
candidates.profiling_evidence: dense A[T,N,N] is the shared mutable state blocking parallel blocks; per-block sparse COO lists reduced once at the end fix RSS and unlock SUP-06. Supply audit B1/B2.
candidates.current_complexity: O(T*N*N) dense resident
candidates.proposed_fix: Each block emits sparse (slot,o,d,val) tuples; reduce-sum at end into the output frames.
candidates.expected_gain: frees ~0.5-1 GiB; unblocks safe block parallelism
candidates.determinism_risk: none - integer sums
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - available/fleet dense T*N grid is contract-mandated (supply_contracts.py:188); the OUTPUT must stay dense, only the accumulator changes. In-service output already sparse via np.nonzero.

candidates.title: Parallelize the 8 disjoint driver-blocks (serial for-loop today)
candidates.profiling_evidence: driver_block_id (667-671) produces disjoint, complete partitions (asserted 748-750,786-787); 8 blocks run serially. Supply audit B2. Likely the ~8x lever for the 16m stage.
candidates.current_complexity: O(n_blocks) serial wall
candidates.proposed_fix: ProcessPool over blocks; depends on SUP-05 (sparse accumulators) to avoid duplicating dense A per worker. Block assignment uses pd.util.hash_array (deterministic default seed).
candidates.expected_gain: near-linear 8x on the 16m stage (with SUP-05)
candidates.extra_memory: per-worker orders slice (avoid pickling full orders - parent pre-partitions)
candidates.parallel_safety: safe - disjoint driver partitions, deterministic hash
candidates.determinism_risk: none - block assignment deterministic; reduction is integer sum
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: none - same integer accumulators

candidates.title: Eliminate per-round full T*M frozen snapshots + isna rescan
candidates.profiling_evidence: Two full T*M float32 copies per hop (source_value=mask, support_src=copy) ~0.53 GiB each, plus a full T*M bool isna matrix per round. Over R=3 ~3.1 GiB transient. TTE audit entries 2-3. Largest transient RSS in TTE.
candidates.current_complexity: O(R * T*M) cells copied per snapshot type x2
candidates.proposed_fix: Maintain a column-wise NaN bitmask updated only on filled columns; use masked views instead of full copies where the source-gate invariant allows.
candidates.expected_gain: large transient RSS reduction in TTE
candidates.determinism_risk: MEDIUM - must keep freeze semantics so hop depth == round (hops==r invariant, tte_contracts.py:179); an in-place masked-view would change which cells act as legs and break source-gate invariants
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: MEDIUM - validated by tte_contracts.validate_tte_outputs (171-182); must keep freeze semantics

candidates.title: Store TTE_raw as float32 instead of float64
candidates.profiling_evidence: df_raw float64 ~1.06 GiB held across imputation; immediately downcasted internally to float32 (tte.py:363). TTE audit entry 5.
candidates.current_complexity: T*M*8 bytes = 1.06 GiB vs 0.53 GiB at float32
candidates.proposed_fix: Write raw as float32.
candidates.expected_gain: halves ~1 GiB RSS
candidates.determinism_risk: changes stored median precision
candidates.output_equivalence_risk: HIGH - raw-float64 contract (tte_contracts.py:61,126) rejects float32; changes stored precision. Needs contract sign-off.
